newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan removes navy chief after corruption talk.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan removes navy chief after corruption talk.

text.p: Pakistan's naval chief, Admiral Mansurul Haque, linked in newspaper reports with possible corruption, has been removed from his job, the government said on Friday.
A brief Defence Ministry announcement said "the government has retired...Admiral Mansurul Haque with immediate effect", suggesting that he would receive retirement benefit such as pension.

The announcement, which did not name any successor, came a day after official sources said Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif had asked Haque to resign and he had agreed to go eight months before completing his three-year tenure.
"The naval chief was directed by the prime minister to resign after reports appeared in the press suggesting his involvement in corruption," one official said on Thursday.
Haque, who took charge of the navy in October 1994, had been criticised in the press over a controversial purchase of three Agosta 90-B submarines from France in a contract signed the same year.
Senior navy officers told select reporters on Wednesday that no kickbacks had been involved in the submarine deal.
Newspapers quoted an unnamed senior naval officer as saying that Haque was ready to face a court martial if any proof of the charges against him was found.

The submarine agreement calls for the first vessel to be wholly built in France and delivered within four years. The second would be assembled in Pakistan and the third would be completely built in Karachi.
